Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're moving ahead with a private offer but our security and operations teams have asked for a documented path to a higher SLA tier (99.9 -> 99.95) as part of the order. Specifically:

- What operational changes, additional capacity reservations, and any contract language are required to guarantee the uplift?
- Will there be an incremental monthly commitment or a one-time setup charge?
- We need a short playbook for cutover and rollback for the upgraded tier (so our SREs can sign off).

I've attached a short checklist (Medivault_SLA_Uplift_Request.pdf). Can you share a private-offer draft and an acceptance playbook we can run by Legal & Procurement?

Goal is to finalize acceptance and signature within two weeks.

Best,

Medivault Health

Subject: Re: Request: SLA tier uplift & private offer paperwork

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for the checklist, and great to hear Medivault is ready to proceed. Short answer: yes, we can support a documented path to 99.95 with a combination of a reserved capacity uplift, a dedicated high-availability scheduling policy, and a contractual SLA amendment.

I've attached our current private-offer draft (RW_Private_Offer_Draft_v3.docx) and a proposed cutover playbook summary. Highlights:

- Operational changes: reserve an additional 2x GPU capacity pool (dedicated) for warm standby, enable cross-region active-passive failover for critical routes, and enable aggressive KV prefix caching for common pipelines.
- Financials: incremental monthly commit equal to a 25% uplift on your current committed spend (we list options for an 18mo or 12mo term). No separate one-time setup if you accept 12mo; a small onboarding fee applies for month-to-month.
- SLA language: proposed amendment adds a targeted 99.95 availability SLO and an incident review cadence; remedies are service credits per quarter (see section 4).
- Cutover playbook (summary): pre-cutover validation, staged traffic ramp (0 -> 25 -> 60 -> 100), canary in secondary region, 30m rollback window per stage. Full playbook in the attachment.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa and I will update the DocuSign-ready private-offer with the SLA amendment and a short mutual action plan.
2) Ben — can you validate the capacity delta and confirm whether the 2x warm standby estimate is sufficient?
3) Alyssa/Legal — if the commercial terms look okay at a high level, we'll circulate the DocuSign link for signatures and share the runbook.

I'll loop in Procurement if we need to adjust invoicing cadence.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: RW_Private_Offer_Draft_v3.docx, SLA-tier-comparison-2027.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: SLA tier uplift & private offer paperwork

Looping in Ben for technical validation and to capture any additional ops requirements. Below are quick notes after my first pass on Logan's draft:

- Agree with 2x warm standby as a starting point, but for Medivault's peak profile I recommend we propose a formal load-test during the trial window and add a soft buffer of +15% to the standby pool.
- Need to call out RPO/RTO expectations for KV cache rebuilds in the SLA appendix; Ops team will want deterministic failover timings.
- Billing: recommend offering an 18-month payment option with a 10% discount vs 12mo to make the uplift easier to swallow for procurement.

Ben — could you review the attached spreadsheet and confirm the estimated incremental GPU-hours and whether the warm standby can live in the same AZ or requires cross-AZ placement? Also flag any maintenance blackout recommendations we should bake into the playbook.

Thanks — will prep an updated private-offer doc once we have Ben's numbers.

—Marissa
VP, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Logan — quick technical check after running the simulation:

- With Medivault's 95th percentile workload profile the 2x warm standby plus +15% buffer looks appropriate. Estimated incremental GPU-hours: ~28k/month for a 12mo term, ~22k/month amortized for an 18mo commitment. Numbers are attached in SLA-tier-comparison-2027.xlsx.
- Warm standby can live cross-AZ within the same region; cross-region is recommended only if they want active-active (not necessary for 99.95 but worth discussing for DR).
- Maintenance blackout: recommend a 2-hour weekly window for kernel/driver updates and a 4-hour monthly full-stack window; build these into the SLA appendix with notification windows.

I'll prep a short technical appendix and send it to Legal for insertion into the private-offer. If Marissa signs off on the commercial terms, Logan can proceed to produce a DocuSign-ready offer.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-tier-comparison-2027.xlsx
